A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DeCo-DETR study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable; relocated algorithms and supplementary material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original OV-COCO and OV-LVIS results, efficiency measurements, component ablations and an appendix user study.

after.justification: V2 retains original benchmark results, efficiency measurements, ablations and the user study, with a revised ablation score.

M1.justification: Section 3.4 changes the teacher distribution from using projected student queries to frozen CLIP region embeddings, and reverses KL(student||teacher) to KL(teacher||student). This is a localized revision within the retained three-component framework. However, appendix Algorithm 2 retains both earlier formulas, leaving the implemented procedure unclear.

E1.justification: Both versions retain OV-COCO, OV-LVIS, the four OVD supervision regimes, and the same user-study and corruption scenarios. Added citations do not introduce evaluated datasets or tasks.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the benchmark tables, efficiency comparisons and user study. OC-OVD's citation changes from Bangalath to Rasheed, but the supplied bibliographies identify the same work; this is not a replacement baseline.

E3.justification: Dataset splits, metrics, backbones, batch size, hardware, query/prototype configurations and the 25-participant study remain unchanged. Adding AP50 subscripts to table headers clarifies metrics already specified in v1, rather than establishing a changed evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: Table 4 revises the evidence for cosine weighting: the reported full-model novel-class score changes from 38.2 to 41.3, increasing its increment over gradient isolation from 0.7 to 3.8 points. The ablation configurations and other sensitivity, corruption and qualitative analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for the detection results. The user-study percentages and average ratings retain the same reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 4 changes the full-model novel-class score from 38.2 to 41.3 without explaining the revision; other table scores remain unchanged. Section 4.3 corrects GFLOP overhead from 5% to 6.8% and parameter overhead from 3% to 7.3%. It also removes the erroneous 56.7% overall-AP figure, while Table 1 retains 53.1 overall AP.

T1.justification: The teacher-distribution and distillation-objective definitions change in v1 Equations 17–18 versus v2 Equations 13–14. Substituting the distribution's input and reversing asymmetric KL divergence are substantive mathematical revisions. No theorem or proof is added; other equation changes are notation, formatting or relocation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about text-encoder-free inference, decoupled learning and competitive open-vocabulary detection. The introduction retains the 3.1–5.8-point and 135 ms claims; changing 'advanced' to 'competitive' does not substantively redefine them.

C2.justification: Interpretations of hierarchical prototypes, gradient isolation, model scaling and the efficiency trade-off remain unchanged. The limitations concerning resource demands, difficult fine-grained or long-tailed categories, and static-image applicability are retained after appendix renumbering.

D1.justification: Table 6 removes the explicit 'Ours' designation from LLaVA-1.5 13B, making the reference LVLM less explicit without establishing a changed model choice. Implementation settings, hardware and the promised release of code, configurations and pretrained models otherwise remain unchanged; the pseudocode is relocated.

R1.justification: V2 adds Xiao et al. (2025) on visual variational autoencoder prompt tuning in the introduction and Shen and Zhang (2025) on disaster-risk prediction in the benchmark overview. Most other bibliography changes consolidate duplicate or publication/preprint entries, without changing the research positioning.

P1.justification: V2 moves Algorithms 1–3 and the localization-stream explanation into Appendix A.3, condenses several mathematical passages, and makes limited wording edits. It removes the acknowledgements and LLM-writing disclosure and consolidates duplicate references. The overall narrative and section sequence remain recognizable.

P2.justification: Existing tables and algorithm boxes are redistributed, including grouping Tables 1–2 together; both figures are unchanged. Several headers gain AP50 subscripts and Table 6 loses its highlighted 'Ours' marker. Table 4 introduces an error by labeling both class-specific columns as novel-class AP.

improvement.justification: V2 corrects resource-overhead arithmetic and streamlines presentation. However, its revised teacher distribution and KL direction conflict with unchanged Algorithm 2, while Table 4 introduces an ambiguous column label and changes the full-model score without explanation. These benefits and new inconsistencies prevent a reliable net judgment of overall quality.
